pieces.eyebrow: The five things, before the call
pieces.title: Write them, then dial

pieces.text: Ask for a reference number for this call and the name of the person you spoke to.

alt: A blank page listing the five things to write before a call (topic, result, reference, two facts, first sentence) beside a note about asking for a reference number.
caption: The five things to have on one page before you dial.

alt: A restart note card with four rows: where you got to, what was missing, the next small piece, and whether it is still needed.
caption: An example note that turns a twenty minute restart into two.

pieces.caption: Copy the booking reference. Order the card by Friday.

alt: A table showing four rows from a nine-row to-do list and where each goes, beside a card saying only two lines are left to look at tomorrow morning.
caption: Example: part of a nine-row list, sorted into today, now, a real date, and parked.

rows: Put the number by the phone

alt: A table turning three looping thoughts into first physical actions, such as finding a renewal letter or writing one line of a reply.
caption: Example: each thought becomes a verb you could watch happen.

steps.what: Pick the task you keep looking at
Do the step and nothing past it
Leave a one-line note, then stop

pieces.text: Find the letter with the claim number on it and put it next to the phone.

alt: A timeline of ten minutes from picking a task to leaving a note, beside a note showing the insurance claim shrunk to one visible first step.
caption: The ten minutes, minute by minute. The claim example is an illustration.

lines.label: Open
lines.text: I'm waiting on a refund that hasn't arrived. Has it been sent?

lines.label: Facts
lines.text: It's $45, for the order on the 3rd.

lines.label: Close
lines.text: Can I have a reference number and your name?

alt: A short refund call script with an opening line, the facts and a closing request, beside a four item checklist of what to get before hanging up.
caption: Example call lines and the four things to get before you hang up.

pieces.eyebrow: What to say about the gap

lines.label: Say
lines.text: This is later than it should be. What do you need from me.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: I have not dealt with this until now. Can you tell me where it stands.

pieces.text: Acknowledge the gap and move to the practical question, unless they ask why.

alt: Two short lines for naming a long delay and asking where things stand, beside a note to skip the explanation unless asked.
caption: Two ways to name the gap in one sentence. Pick the one closest to how you feel.

items: Write down details you would hold
Do clear-head tasks on clear days

pieces.text: What happens after you ignore it for three weeks? A good system is still roughly right.

alt: A checklist of five adjustments for low-capacity days, with two ticked, beside a note about how a system should hold up after three weeks of being ignored.
caption: Adjustments that do not depend on knowing why, or on trying harder.

right.label: Stuck at start
items: Put what you need in front

pieces.text: Is there something you would rather be doing? If not, starting may be the wall.

alt: Two columns of things to try, one for choosing something nicer and one for being unable to start, beside a note with the question that tells them apart.
caption: Tendencies, not a test. Plenty of people land in the middle.

pieces.text: Treat the repeat prescription cycle as a recurring appointment, not a task.

alt: A blank page for keeping clinic, prescription and pharmacy references and a written history together, beside a note about repeat prescriptions.
caption: A page to keep the references together. Your prescriber sets the schedule.

pieces.question: Who is waiting on this?
options: A person is waiting on you

pieces.text: Out of sight is not lost. Write them down and stop looking tonight.

alt: A card sorting late tasks into three piles: a person waiting, a date attached, or no one waiting, beside a note that the rest can be put away tonight.
caption: Put each thing in one pile instead of ranking the lot.

steps.what: One box or one shelf, then stop
Open each item. Do not act yet.
A person, a date, or no one

pieces.eyebrow: If ten minutes is too much
pieces.caption: Open one envelope. That is a real start.

alt: A four-step timeline for a ten minute pass through a paperwork pile, beside a card saying one envelope is a real start.
caption: Open, sort, then choose one small piece.

lines.label: Say it
lines.text: I can't host in March. I'm sorry to give you the news by phone.

lines.label: Stop
lines.text: Say nothing more. A pause feels long and isn't.

lines.label: Hold
lines.text: I understand it's disappointing. My answer is still no.

pieces.text: You're allowed to ask for a minute, and to say you'll call back.

alt: A short script card with three lines for saying no on a call, say it, pause, hold your answer, beside a note that you can ask for a minute.
caption: An example of the order: news first, then a pause.

steps.what: Send it. Note the date and the ask.
Try a different route. Ask for a date.
Add a second person or address.

pieces.text: Read it once against the checks, then send it.

alt: A four-step chase plan for an email that got no reply, day 0 to day 15, beside a note to read the draft once before sending.
caption: Example days; shorten them if a deadline is close.

pieces.text: Pick one step to happen today. Write the next one down.

alt: A three-row table pairing a task with its first physical step, dentist, insurance claim and spare room, beside a note to pick one step for today.
caption: Example steps; copy the shape, not the task.

pieces.text: On a bad week, open the pile and pick one thing. That counts as a reset.

alt: A comparison of a reset that needs a good week and one that survives a bad week, beside a note that opening the pile and picking one thing counts.
caption: The ten minute reset works the same after a missed week.

pieces.text: Do not reset it. Find the one page that still counts and keep only that.

alt: A table of four things a planner needs and what happens in a hard week, beside a note to keep one page instead of starting over.
caption: What usually breaks, in a hard week.

steps.what: Write the bill with its date attached
Pick whether you want one, and which dates
So it does not land at a bad time
A short look at the next few days

pieces.text: A reminder that says what it is about can be read by anyone nearby.

alt: A four-step timeline for keeping bill due dates in front of you without remembering, beside a note about keeping reminders private.
caption: Four of the five steps in the guide.

pieces.text: Name one exact time, not a window, and put it where you will see it.

alt: A table turning four vague plans into exact times, beside a note to name one time and keep it visible.
caption: Example: vague plans and their exact versions.
